question: Most things that 'go viral' online mainly spread in which way?
options: Person to person, like a virus
answer: Mostly from a few big broadcasts: a celebrity, a big account or a news site shares it, and many people see it at once. Thompson cites research on millions of online cascades showing that long chains of person-to-person sharing are rare. Popularity usually has a megaphone behind it.
move: Behind most 'viral' hits, look for the megaphone.
trap: 'Person to person': the word 'viral' makes us picture contagion.
simply: We imagine a video spreads friend to friend, like a cold. Usually one famous account shares it and millions see it at once.
why: It changes how you read online popularity: a trend is often a few big accounts' choice, not the crowd's.

book.title: Hit Makers
book.author: Derek Thompson
book.badge: By a senior editor at The Atlantic

reference: Derek Thompson, Hit Makers: The Science of Popularity in an Age of Distraction (Penguin Press, 2017), ch. 7
